evidence.location: line 40, Acceptance details (with section 0 line 4 and section 2 line 10)
evidence.observation: The only signature test is 'For each registered family check the signature against the family's expected operands and host, including their order.' Section 2 promises only 'registered constraint signatures', and section 0 claims 'a complete read-only inventory of the resolved model'. Nothing names modality, status or family parameters. The named fixture tests/fixtures/models/full_vocabulary.orm.yaml has constraints with 'modality: deontic' and 'status: proposed', and a value constraint with 'allowed: ["M", "F", "X"]'. A signature that drops these, or merges a deontic proposed constraint with an alethic confirmed one, passes the stated test.

concerns.recommendation: Define the per-family signature to cover modality and every meaning-bearing parameter: allowed values and ranges, ring variant, frequency bounds, preferred. Either include status or exclude it explicitly. Extend the coverage test so that changing each such field changes the rendered record.
concerns.title: Constraint signatures are tested only for operands and host, so lost modality or parameters go undetected

evidence.observation: Line 40 says 'GC1 returns the exact object, fact and authored constraint IDs supplied by the loader' and 'Assert equality of the fixture's authored IDs before and after reordering'. Line 42 says 'Sort object and fact records by ID, subtype pairs by endpoints, constraints by canonical signature.' In this repo, src/gnd/schema/orm-meta.schema.json makes constraint 'id' optional (constraint_common), and none of the 14 top-level constraints in full_vocabulary.orm.yaml has an id. So the reorder assertion is empty for constraints. Any two constraints with equal canonical signatures (duplicates, or ones that differ only in excluded fields) tie, which leaves their output order, and the bytes, dependent on authored order.

concerns.recommendation: Say how a constraint without an ID is identified in the view: either the signature is its identity, or duplicates are merged or refused. Require a total order, for example the signature followed by the full canonical record. Add a fixture with ID-less constraints whose signatures collide, and assert byte equality after reordering it.
concerns.title: Constraint identity and sort order are undefined when constraints have no authored ID

evidence.observation: 'Bind expected_model_sha256 to the root bytes from which the view was loaded and reauthenticate pins through the existing evolution workflow.'

The host record lists 'actual prompt scope, full or partial status, exact view digest, queries, inspected IDs, chosen action and source occurrence'. It has no root sha256. Line 44 requires that 'raw root identity changes after an evidence-only edit even when the view digest stays equal', so the view digest cannot stand in for root identity. Neither 'gnd verbalize model MODEL --for-growth' nor 'gnd.api.verbalize_model(MODEL, for_growth=True)' is said to report the root sha256 or the include pins it loaded. A host that hashes the root after rendering binds the proposal to bytes the agent never saw, and the evolution stale-state check still passes.

concerns.recommendation: Have both surfaces report the sha256 of the root bytes they actually read, plus the verified include pins. Keep these outside the view digest, for example in an envelope or a separate output. Add them to the host record. Test that an edit between rendering and proposal makes evolution refuse.
concerns.title: The root bytes behind a view are not captured with it, so a later edit can pass the stale-state check

evidence.observation: Section 2 says 'Use a view digest for replay'. Line 42 says 'SHA-256 covers all resulting UTF-8 bytes' and requires 'unescaped Unicode, and a single final LF'. GC2 asks for 'CLI/API byte parity from an installed wheel'. The plan does not say whether the digest is embedded in the JSON (which would be circular with 'covers all resulting UTF-8 bytes'), printed by the CLI, or computed by the host. It also does not say whether the API returns str or bytes. The existing src/gnd/api.py verbalize_model returns str.

concerns.recommendation: State that the digest is the sha256 of the exact rendered bytes, never embedded in them, and say which surface reports it. Specify that the API's str.encode('utf-8') equals the CLI's stdout bytes. Have the CLI write bytes to stdout.buffer, so there is no extra print() newline, no CRLF translation and no locale encoding. Test with a non-ASCII reading under a non-UTF-8 PYTHONIOENCODING.
concerns.title: The digest's location and the CLI/API byte encoding are unspecified

evidence.observation: 'GC2 exposes gnd verbalize model MODEL --for-growth and gnd.api.verbalize_model(MODEL, for_growth=True).' Line 40 requires 'Unresolved includes refuse before output' and line 46 requires binding to 'the root bytes from which the view was loaded'. In this repo, src/gnd/api.py declares verbalize_model(model: str | os.PathLike[str] | Model) -> str, and the checking_service resolver returns an in-memory Model unchanged with no coordinate, so no root bytes or include pins exist for that input. The plan does not say what for_growth=True does with a Model object.

concerns.recommendation: Either refuse a Model object when for_growth=True with a documented TypeError, or define the identity such a view carries and state that CLI/API parity applies to path input only. Add a test for the chosen behaviour.
concerns.title: for_growth=True with an in-memory Model has no root bytes or pins, and its behaviour is unspecified

evidence.location: lines 40 and 42; section 2 line 10; section 5 line 21
evidence.observation: 'The top-level format field is exactly gnd-growth-view-v1.' and 'Family registration growth must cause the coverage test to fail until a signature case exists.' Section 2 says 'Use a view digest for replay.' Nothing states when the bytes for an unchanged model may change under v1, such as a new family, a new field or a renderer fix. The host record in section 5 does not include the GND version or the format, so replaying a recorded digest under another GND version can silently fail to match.

concerns.recommendation: Add a rule that any byte change for an unchanged model needs a new format value, or that a digest is replayable only with the same GND version. Record the format and GND version in the host record. Add a golden-bytes snapshot of the v1 fixture view so that drift fails a test.
concerns.title: No v1 compatibility rule protects replay by view digest across GND versions

evidence.observation: The contract lists what is exposed and says 'Exclude author evidence, samples, notes and rationale.' rejected_proposals is in neither list. The named fixture full_vocabulary.orm.yaml has a 'rejected_proposals:' section: a ring 'intransitive' entry on employee_reports_to_employee with a rejection_reason. If the allowlist drops it, an agent told to 'inspect the complete inventory for that shape' cannot see that the shape was already rejected, and may propose it again.

concerns.recommendation: Decide explicitly whether rejected-proposal signatures are part of the inventory, without their rationale or reason text. Then add that decision to the field allowlist test and the evidence-sentinel test.
concerns.title: Whether rejected proposals appear in the view is undecided

evidence.observation: The plan says 'Any number of partial misses alone is insufficient to propose novelty.' and 'Check that the first search yields zero rows, the next finds the known included fact, and ambiguous evidence yields defer with no added fact.' It also says 'Check reversed role bindings are ineligible for reuse.' Section 3 assigns 'passage selection, search strategy and prompt budgeting' to the host, and section 7 excludes search. The scripted example therefore only shows its own script behaving. No stated test fails when a host proposes novelty after partial misses alone, and it is not said whether the reversed-binding eligibility check is GND code or example code.

concerns.recommendation: Ship a small checker over the host JSON record, in the example or in the packaged-guide tests. It should flag a propose decision whose record shows only partial-scope inspection, and a reuse whose role bindings are reversed. Add a negative case where it fails. State which component owns the eligibility check.
concerns.title: The novelty and reuse-eligibility rules are tested only by the example's own scripted path

evidence.observation: Section 2 says 'Preserve meaningful order and use deterministic ordering elsewhere'. Line 42 says 'Retain authored role order and asymmetric operand sides'. Line 40's reorder test asserts only 'equality of the fixture's authored IDs before and after reordering', not equal bytes. The plan never says which operand lists are ordered and which are sets. The fixture's external uniqueness and mandatory-disjunctive constraints list role_refs that are sets semantically. If they are kept in authored order, a harmless reorder changes the bytes. If they are sorted, the same rule applied to subset or exclusion operands would lose direction.

concerns.recommendation: For each registered family, declare which operand lists are ordered and which are sets. Make the reorder test assert byte equality when set operands are permuted, and a changed record when ordered or asymmetric operands are swapped.
concerns.title: Which operand lists are sets and which are ordered is undefined, and reordering is checked only by IDs

evidence.observation: The criterion is 'A compact rendering must be strictly smaller in UTF-8 bytes than both the original full_vocabulary.orm.yaml fixture and the ordinary review rendering of that same model.' In the repo that fixture is a version 1 model of 16927 bytes with no includes. Much of it is comments, provenance and rationale, which the view drops by design. So 'strictly smaller' passes for nearly any JSON, and the include-backed GC2 example is never measured.

concerns.recommendation: Also report bytes for the include-backed example, together with bytes per object, fact and constraint record. Or compare against a baseline that serializes only the allowlisted fields, so that verbose keys or duplicated readings creeping back show up as a regression.
concerns.title: The compactness check is a strictly-smaller bar on one fixture with no includes

response.summary: The two-phase scope is coherent: there is one renderer, the default output stays unchanged, the view digest is kept apart from root-byte binding, and the retry and deferral checks are concrete. But several obligations can pass their stated tests while still being wrong. The constraint-signature check covers only operands and host. Constraint identity and ordering are undefined for constraints that have no ID, which is every constraint in the named fixture. The surfaces do not hand back the root sha256 the view was rendered from. The digest's location and the CLI/API byte encoding are unspecified, and v1 has no compatibility rule. No blocking defects.

evidence.observation: The plan promises "registered constraint signatures" but tests each signature against only the family's "expected operands and host, including their order." The model format also has semantic fields such as cardinality bounds, ring variants, status and modality. Two constraints can share operands and host while differing in those fields; the stated test could pass even if the compact view makes them indistinguishable.

concerns.recommendation: Define the semantic fields retained for each registered family, including status and modality, and test pairs that differ only in one such field.
concerns.title: Constraint signatures lack a testable semantic completeness contract

response.summary: The plan states a clear v1 contract and honest scope limits, but two obligations that carry its identity and compatibility claims are not demonstrable from the stated evidence: record ordering uses keys the plan never shows to be unique, so the deterministic-bytes and replay-digest claim is unproven, and the CLI surface has no stated byte-exactness rule even though parity and SHA-256 digests are the product's currency. Several acceptance items are weaker than the contract sentences they verify (disclosure by sentinel strings only, subtype direction unasserted, no golden bytes for the growth view, one miss-then-hit for an unbounded retry protocol).

evidence.observation: "A compact rendering must be strictly smaller in UTF-8 bytes than both the original full_vocabulary.orm.yaml fixture and the ordinary review rendering of that same model. Report all three counts. No cross-corpus threshold is claimed." The acceptance test is a strict inequality on one fixture, so any reduction (even a handful of bytes) passes GC1 while the motivating claim of issue 295 (line 7: "compact prompt context") would remain essentially undemonstrated.

The risk controls say only "Measure actual UTF-8 bytes and confine comparisons to the measured fixture" — a control against overclaiming across corpora, but nothing guards against a trivial pass on the measured fixture (no minimum relative margin or recorded ratio gate).

concerns.recommendation: Strengthen the line-42 acceptance to require a stated minimum relative reduction (or explicitly declare the strict inequality a serialization sanity floor and record the measured three-way byte counts plus ratio as a tracked limitation at close, per line 33's 'Record measured sizes').
concerns.title: Compactness acceptance is a bare strict inequality on one fixture with no margin, so a negligible reduction passes

response.summary: The plan is internally consistent and each product obligation (canonical gnd-growth-view-v1 bytes, stable loader-supplied IDs, deterministic ordering, evidence exclusion, root-byte authentication of includes, default-output compatibility, and host-driven retry/deferral) is paired with a concrete, falsifiable verification in GC1/GC2 or the runnable example. response.summary: Digest verified. Schema identity, compatibility and retry obligations are mostly paired with falsifiable evidence: root-byte and pin checks defeat evidence-only edits that preserve the view digest, default output is snapshot-verified, CLI/API parity is checked from an installed wheel, and the miss-hit-defer loop is exercised by a runnable example. Residual gaps: the any-number-of-partial-misses novelty guard is stronger than anything the stated evidence can falsify, the GC1 empty-model case has no acceptance-level check to reconcile against, reference-mode and subtype-link exposure is never asserted, the compactness gate compares against an unpinned fixture, and the constraint sort key canonical signature is undefined while document serialization is fully specified.

criteria: Can each product obligation be implemented and falsified with the stated evidence?
